paragraphs: Long sequences make language-model inference expensive partly because the key-value cache grows with the context. Cache eviction reduces this storage by removing elements judged less important to generation. The paper identifies a weakness in existing approaches: they typically distribute compression budgets uniformly across attention heads, even though those heads exhibit different attention patterns.

Ada-KV replaces that uniform allocation with a budget chosen separately for each head. Its foundation is a theoretical upper bound on the difference between attention outputs before and after eviction. This bound clarifies the objective underlying earlier eviction methods and guides the new allocation strategy. The approach is designed to integrate with existing eviction methods, making allocation an independently useful component.

Evaluations cover 13 Ruler datasets and 16 LongBench datasets, with both question-aware and question-agnostic settings. The authors report substantial generation-quality improvements over existing methods. These findings support treating differences among attention heads as relevant to cache compression: deciding how much capacity each head receives can improve the quality preserved by eviction.
neurips-2025-ada-kv-optimizing-kv-cache-.tldr: Ada-KV improves cache eviction by allocating compression budgets adaptively across attention heads using a theoretical attention-error bound.

paragraphs: Reading long documents requires an LLM to organize more information than it can conveniently use at once. This paper approaches that problem through an explicit memory system. Drawing on Piaget's constructivist theory, it proposes three design principles: structured knowledge organization, flexible incorporation of information, and dynamic adjustment as information accumulates.

CAM implements these principles with an incremental clustering algorithm whose groups can overlap. This structure supports hierarchical summaries while allowing new batches of information to enter the memory during operation. The combination matters because a reading agent needs both an organized account of what it has encountered and a way to incorporate additional material into that account.

When answering a query, CAM adaptively explores its memory to activate relevant information for the response. The authors report advantages in both performance and efficiency over existing approaches across question answering, query-based summarization, and claim verification on long texts. The contribution connects a proposed memory-design framework to a working system and evaluates its usefulness across several forms of reading comprehension.
neurips-2025-cam-a-constructivist-view-o.tldr: CAM organizes and updates document memory through overlapping clusters, improving long-text reading performance and efficiency in the reported evaluations.

paragraphs: Neural networks can learn different internal representations even when trained on the same task and data. Training randomness, architecture, and inductive biases all contribute to these differences. The paper investigates how to connect such representations by using the geometry they share, building on earlier observations that relative distances can survive across latent spaces with some distortion.

The central assumption is that the models approximately describe the same underlying manifold: a shared lower-dimensional structure within the data. The proposed representation uses a pullback metric to capture intrinsic geometry within each latent space. Under this shared-manifold view, the authors demonstrate that geometric structure can precisely capture transformations between representation spaces trained on similar distributions.

The method is designed to scale to large models and is evaluated on model stitching and retrieval. Experiments include autoencoders and vision foundation discriminative models across architectures, datasets, pretraining schemes, and modalities. These evaluations examine whether geometrically grounded representations can support useful connections between models whose internal coordinates differ. The shared-manifold assumption is central to interpreting the proposed correspondence.
neurips-2025-connecting-neural-models-la.tldr: Relative geodesic representations use shared manifold geometry to connect neural models' latent spaces under an approximate common-manifold assumption.

paragraphs: MRI reconstruction models can lose performance when scanners or acquisition protocols differ from those encountered previously. Adapting the model at test time can address these distribution shifts, but repeated training creates computational costs. The paper also identifies over-smoothing as a risk for self-supervised approaches when little data is available.

D2SA divides adaptation into two stages with different responsibilities. First, an MRI implicit neural representation learns information shared across a patient's slices. Adjustments to means and variances model the patient's particular distribution shift. Second, adaptation focuses on individual slices: a learnable anisotropic diffusion module refines outputs from convolutional layers that remain frozen. This stage is intended to prevent over-smoothing while reducing computation.

The division allows patient-level structure and slice-level refinement to contribute separately to reconstruction. Across five MRI distribution shifts, the authors report improved performance and faster convergence, with the method integrating into various self-supervised learning frameworks. The findings support this two-stage organization as an effective way to adapt reconstruction models under the diverse conditions examined.
neurips-2025-d2sa-dual-stage-distributio.tldr: D2SA combines patient-level distribution adaptation with efficient slice-level refinement to improve MRI reconstruction under distribution shifts.

paragraphs: Reinforcement learning is a central technique for eliciting complex reasoning from language models, but reproducing leading results can be difficult when training details remain hidden. This paper addresses that reproducibility problem by presenting an openly released algorithm, training system, and processed dataset for reinforcement learning at large scale.

The algorithm is called Decoupled Clip and Dynamic Sampling Policy Optimization, or DAPO. The authors describe four key techniques that make their large-scale training successful and release an implementation built on the verl framework. Sharing the implementation alongside a curated dataset makes both the training procedure and its data available for subsequent research.

Using the Qwen2.5-32B base model, the system achieves 50 points on AIME 2024. That result provides a concrete demonstration of the released system's mathematical-reasoning performance in the reported setting. The contribution combines an algorithmic proposal with the practical components needed to investigate and reproduce this kind of training, giving researchers an accessible foundation for further large-scale LLM reinforcement-learning work.
neurips-2025-dapo-an-open-source-llm-rei.tldr: DAPO releases a large-scale LLM reinforcement-learning algorithm, system, and dataset, reporting 50 points on AIME 2024 with Qwen2.5-32B.

paragraphs: The Distributional Principal Autoencoder aims to reconstruct a data distribution while producing encodings with interpretability resembling principal components. This paper gives theoretical guarantees for both goals. Its first result connects the geometry of optimal encoder level sets to the data-distribution score, making a precise link between representation geometry and distributional structure.

The authors derive this connection in closed form. It explains the model's observed ability to separate factors of variation and enables recovery of the score directly from samples. For data following a Boltzmann distribution, they demonstrate an application to the Müller–Brown potential: a single model fit yields an approximation of a minimum free-energy path.

The second result concerns intrinsic dimension. If data lies on a manifold that the encoder can approximate, latent components beyond that manifold's dimension are conditionally independent of the data distribution and add no information. This provides a way to reveal the intrinsic dimension. Together, the results establish how one model can learn distributional structure and identify dimensionality, with the dimensionality guarantee explicitly depending on the stated manifold and encoder condition.
neurips-2025-distributional-autoencoders.tldr: The paper proves links between distributional autoencoder geometry, distribution scores, and intrinsic dimension under a stated manifold-approximation condition.

paragraphs: A bandit algorithm repeatedly chooses among actions while learning which rewards are best. Earlier theory showed that the Stochastic Gradient Bandit policy eventually converges to an optimal policy with a constant learning rate, and that sufficiently small rates can achieve logarithmic regret. This paper asks how the learning rate changes regret along the way, beyond eventual convergence.

For two actions, the authors identify a sharp threshold that scales with the suboptimality gap, the reward difference separating the inferior action from the best one. Below the threshold, the algorithm achieves logarithmic regret on all instances. Above it, some instances can produce polynomial regret. The latter is a possibility established by the result, rather than a claim about every instance.

For a general number of actions K, the learning rate must also scale inversely with K to avoid polynomial regret. The results show why choosing a constant rate requires knowing or estimating the reward gap to ensure logarithmic regret. New techniques for regret upper bounds further develop the theoretical analysis of gradient-based bandit policies.
neurips-2025-does-stochastic-gradient-re.tldr: Stochastic Gradient Bandit's regret depends sharply on its learning rate, with rates above a gap-dependent threshold permitting polynomial regret.

paragraphs: An intervention's most important effects may appear during rare events, where observational data offers few examples. The paper focuses on estimating those effects, using extreme climate events as a motivating case. Standard causal-effect methods primarily address frequently observed outcomes, while the extreme-event setting requires some extrapolation beyond the available observations.

The proposed framework combines treatment-effect estimation with Extreme Value Theory, which studies statistical behavior in extreme regimes. Specifically, it uses multivariate regular variation to model extremities. This modeling choice supplies the structure for defining and estimating causal effects associated with rare events, addressing a different target from effects measured mainly in the ordinary part of a distribution.

The authors develop a consistent estimator and provide a non-asymptotic performance analysis, examining estimation behavior with finite data as well as its large-sample target. Synthetic and semi-synthetic experiments illustrate the estimator's performance. The contribution is a mathematical framework for the necessary extrapolation, supported by theoretical analysis and controlled data examples, for interventions whose relevant consequences arise in scarce extreme observations.
neurips-2025-estimation-of-treatment-eff.tldr: The paper uses Extreme Value Theory to estimate treatment effects in rare-event regimes, with consistency and finite-sample analysis.

paragraphs: Post-training datasets help language models follow instructions and develop useful skills, but understanding which data choices improve performance is difficult. Many leading datasets are inaccessible, and rigorous comparisons of open alternatives are computationally expensive. This paper directly compares two prominent open datasets, Tulu-3-SFT-Mix and SmolTalk, to connect their composition and quality with downstream results.

Using the Magpie framework, the authors annotate individual samples for conversation structure, task category, input quality, and response quality. These annotations expose similarities and differences that a dataset's overall size would not reveal. The analysis then informs a curation recipe for combining data into a new mixture called TuluTalk.

TuluTalk contains 14% fewer samples than either source dataset while matching or exceeding their performance on key benchmarks. This finding supports the value of deliberate data selection in the studied setting: a smaller, curated mixture can retain or improve measured performance. The authors release both annotated source datasets and TuluTalk so that the analysis and resulting mixture can support further post-training research.
neurips-2025-fixing-it-in-post-a-compara.tldr: A detailed comparison of two open post-training datasets produces TuluTalk, a 14% smaller mixture that matches or improves key benchmark performance.

paragraphs: Graph matching seeks corresponding nodes in two graphs and is commonly formulated as a difficult discrete quadratic assignment problem. Continuous relaxations make optimization more manageable by enlarging the set of permitted solutions. The paper identifies two resulting problems: sensitivity to numerical scale and a mismatch between the geometry of the relaxed domain and the original discrete one.

FRAM addresses these problems by reformulating projection as a Frobenius-regularized linear assignment problem. A tunable regularization term controls feasible-region inflation and provides numerical scale invariance. The authors develop a scaling algorithm for doubly stochastic normalization, then use its computational properties to construct a theoretically grounded accelerated algorithm that mixes numerical precisions.

The complete method approximates quadratic assignment through a sequence of these regularized linear assignment problems. CPU experiments report that FRAM consistently outperforms all evaluated baselines. On GPUs, mixed-precision FRAM achieves up to a 370-fold speedup over its own FP64 CPU implementation without sacrificing accuracy. That comparison demonstrates the combined computational benefit of the GPU and mixed-precision implementation against the stated CPU reference.
neurips-2025-fram-frobenius-regularized-.tldr: FRAM improves graph-matching relaxation and reports up to 370-fold GPU speedup over its FP64 CPU implementation without accuracy loss.

paragraphs: The Segment Anything Model needs to remain useful when input images are degraded, especially in applications such as robotics and autonomous driving. This paper targets robustness while prioritizing parameter efficiency, sensitivity to the particular corruption in an image, and compatibility with standard training protocols. Preserving SAM's generalization capability is also a stated design goal.

Gated-rank adaptation adds lightweight adapters to intermediate layers while keeping SAM itself frozen. Each adapter contains rank-one components that a learned gate selectively activates based on the input. This changes the effective rank of the adapter's weight matrix dynamically, allowing the adaptation to respond at a fine-grained level to the image being processed.

The resulting GaRA-SAM model significantly outperforms prior work across all robust segmentation benchmarks reported in the study. On ACDC, a dataset of real corrupted images, the improvement over the previous best intersection-over-union score reaches 21.3 percentage points. These results support input-dependent adapter capacity as a useful mechanism for improving corruption robustness while retaining the underlying model's generalization capability.
neurips-2025-gara-sam-robustifying-segme.tldr: GaRA-SAM uses input-dependent gated adapters to improve segmentation robustness, gaining up to 21.3 IoU percentage points on ACDC.

paragraphs: Label shift means class frequencies change between source and target data while the distribution of inputs within each class stays the same. Estimating the new frequencies is difficult when target labels are unavailable. Classical black-box estimators invert an empirical confusion matrix from a frozen classifier, producing a point estimate that overlooks sampling uncertainty and relationships among classes.

The proposed Bayesian estimator models uncertainty in both target class proportions and the confusion matrix. It places Laplacian–Gaussian priors on target log-proportions and confusion-matrix columns, using a label-similarity graph to connect related quantities. The resulting posterior can be handled with Hamiltonian Monte Carlo or a faster block Newton–CG procedure.

The paper proves identifiability, contraction at an N-to-the-minus-one-half rate, and variance bounds that become smaller with greater algebraic connectivity of the graph. It also establishes robustness to Laplacian misspecification. An information-geometric interpretation shows how the method generalizes existing shift estimators. These guarantees give a theoretical account of uncertainty and graph-based smoothing within the stated label-shift setting.
neurips-2025-graphsmoothed-bayesian-blac.tldr: A graph-smoothed Bayesian label-shift estimator jointly models class proportions and classifier uncertainty, with theoretical estimation guarantees.

paragraphs: Time-series foundation models can forecast across different domains, but their hallucinations have received comparatively little study. This paper defines hallucination for zero-shot forecasting by asking whether a prediction exhibits dynamics different from those in its input context. That definition focuses attention on whether the generated continuation preserves the behavior of the observed sequence.

The study identifies loss of context information in hidden states during forward propagation as the primary source of these hallucinations. The authors then develop methods to locate signal subspaces inside the models and intervene to amplify the information they contain. This connects the proposed failure mechanism to an intervention directed at the model's internal representations.

Extensive experiments show that the intervention reduces hallucinations and improves forecasting performance. The authors also derive a signal-strength measure from the identified subspaces that strongly predicts both hallucination behavior and forecast performance. The work therefore offers both a way to change model behavior and an internal diagnostic associated with forecast reliability in the evaluated zero-shot setting.
neurips-2025-investigating-hallucination.tldr: The study links forecasting hallucinations to lost context information and reduces them by amplifying signal subspaces inside time-series models.

paragraphs: Compiler optimizations improve program performance through transformations of intermediate representations, or IRs. Maintaining manually written transformation rules becomes demanding as compilers grow more complex. This paper targets a barrier to using LLMs for that work: insufficient training data showing diverse, relevant IR transformations from real programs.

IR-OptSet provides 170,000 LLVM IR samples drawn from open-source repositories across eight optimization domains. It defines two tasks, code analysis and optimized code generation, and includes tools for checking correctness, measuring performance, and expanding the dataset. Its emphasis on optimization-sensitive samples aims to expose models to examples that teach useful transformation strategies.

Fine-tuning three representative LLMs improves accuracy on both tasks. An LLM fine-tuned with IR-OptSet also produces better performance than a traditional compiler using the -O3 option in 64 test cases. That result concerns those cases, rather than a general replacement claim. Further analysis finds greater transformation diversity and representativeness than three existing IR datasets, supporting the dataset's role in studying learned compiler optimization.
neurips-2025-ir-optset-an-optimization-s.tldr: IR-OptSet supplies 170,000 optimization-focused LLVM IR samples and improves LLM code analysis and optimization in reported experiments.

paragraphs: Mixture-of-Experts language models organize computation into modules, but their sparse execution creates hardware challenges. Memory locality, communication overhead, and underused computing resources can reduce the efficiency that modular computation promises. Mozart addresses these issues by designing the training algorithm and hardware organization together for 3.5D wafer-scale chiplet architectures.

On the algorithm side, Mozart assigns experts to support efficient all-to-all communication within the package. A fine-grained scheduler streams tokens and experts to improve overlap between communication and computation. On the architecture side, it places different modules together on specialized chiplets using a 2.5D NoP-Tree topology and hierarchical memory structure.

These components coordinate where computation happens, how data moves, and when operations run. The design uses the modular structure of chiplets to support the modular structure of the model. Evaluation across three popular MoE models reports significant efficiency improvements, including more effective parallelization and resource utilization. The findings concern the combined algorithm–hardware framework for the targeted chiplet architecture.
neurips-2025-mozart-modularized-and-effi.tldr: Mozart jointly designs expert placement, scheduling, and chiplet architecture to improve the efficiency of large-scale MoE training.

paragraphs: SVG graphics are useful in design because they remain editable and independent of output resolution. Generating complex, high-quality SVGs is nevertheless challenging: existing approaches can produce expensive, unstructured outputs or remain restricted to simple monochrome icons. OmniSVG addresses this problem through a unified generation framework built on pretrained vision-language models.

The method converts SVG commands and coordinates into discrete tokens. This representation separates structural logic from low-level geometry, supporting efficient training while preserving the ability to express complex SVG structures. The framework uses that representation for end-to-end multimodal generation, connecting the underlying vision-language model to a structured graphics output.

The paper also introduces MMSVG-2M, a dataset containing two million richly annotated SVG assets, and a standardized protocol for evaluating conditional SVG generation. Experiments report better performance than existing methods and indicate potential for professional design workflows. Together, the model, data, and evaluation protocol support both generation of more complex vector graphics and more consistent assessment of progress on the task.
neurips-2025-omnisvg-a-unified-scalable-.tldr: OmniSVG generates complex vector graphics through discrete SVG tokens and introduces a two-million-asset dataset with a standardized evaluation protocol.

paragraphs: Ordering-based causal discovery searches for an ordering compatible with a causal graph, offering an alternative to combinatorial graph search. Under additive-noise assumptions, score-based methods depend on accurately estimating diagonal entries of the log-density Hessian. Existing estimators can be expensive, while the diffusion-based DiffAN approach encounters numerical instability from second-order derivatives of score models.

SciNO is a probabilistic generative model operating in smooth function spaces. It is designed to approximate the required Hessian diagonal stably while preserving structural information during score modeling. Relative to DiffAN, experiments report average reductions in order divergence of 42.7% on synthetic graphs and 31.5% on real-world datasets, while retaining memory efficiency and scalability.

The paper also introduces a probabilistic control algorithm that combines SciNO's probability estimates with priors from autoregressive models. This joins data-driven ordering evidence with semantic information for causal reasoning. The authors report improved LLM causal reasoning without additional fine-tuning or prompt engineering. The overall contribution links more stable statistical estimation to a mechanism for informing autoregressive causal judgments.
neurips-2025-score-informed-neural-opera.tldr: SciNO stabilizes score-based causal ordering and combines its probability estimates with autoregressive priors to improve LLM causal reasoning.

paragraphs: A visually convincing generated video may still fail to follow the controls needed in professional filmmaking. Stable Cinemetrics evaluates those requirements through four separate hierarchical taxonomies: Setup, Event, Lighting, and Camera. Together, they contain 76 fine-grained control nodes grounded in industry practice, making filmmaking instructions explicit targets for assessment.

The authors build a prompt benchmark around these taxonomies and automate prompt categorization and evaluation-question generation. This allows each control dimension to be assessed independently. A human study covers more than ten models and 20,000 videos, with annotations from a pool of more than 80 film professionals.

The analysis finds substantial gaps even among the strongest evaluated models, particularly for events and camera controls. To make this assessment more scalable, the authors train a vision-language evaluator aligned with expert annotations; it outperforms existing zero-shot baselines. The framework provides a structured way to distinguish visual quality from success at specific cinematic instructions and to identify which professional controls still need improvement.
neurips-2025-stable-cinemetrics-structur.tldr: Stable Cinemetrics evaluates 76 professional filmmaking controls and finds substantial weaknesses in generated events and camera behavior.

paragraphs: Recurrent models compress history into a fixed-size state, while attention directly models relationships across tokens in its context window. Attention's quadratic cost constrains the length of that window. Titans combines attention with a neural long-term memory module that learns to retain historical context, allowing current-context processing to draw on information from much earlier.

The authors describe attention as short-term memory because it models dependencies accurately within a limited context. The neural module serves as a more persistent memory and supports fast, parallelizable training. They introduce three architectural variants that explore how to incorporate these two components into a single model family.

Experiments evaluate Titans on language modeling, common-sense reasoning, and time-series tasks, reporting effectiveness relative to baselines. Needle-in-haystack experiments also show effective scaling to larger context windows. The central architectural contribution is a division of memory responsibilities: attention handles direct relationships in the current context, while learned neural memory supplies access to historical information beyond that immediate window.
neurips-2025-titans-learning-to-memorize.tldr: Titans combines attention with learned long-term neural memory to use historical information and scale effectively to larger contexts in reported tests.

paragraphs: Autonomous vehicles can struggle to perceive objects hidden by occlusions or beyond their sensing range. Cooperative perception addresses this by bringing together observations from multiple locations. This paper introduces V2X-Radar to fill a dataset gap: existing cooperative-perception resources largely emphasize cameras and LiDAR, despite the use of 4D radar for robust single-vehicle perception in adverse weather.

The data comes from a connected vehicle platform and an intelligent roadside unit equipped with 4D radar, LiDAR, and multi-view cameras. Collection covers sunny and rainy weather, daytime, dusk, nighttime, and challenging scenarios. The dataset contains 20,000 LiDAR frames, 40,000 camera images, 20,000 radar data items, and 350,000 annotated boxes across five categories.

Three sub-datasets support cooperative, roadside, and single-vehicle perception, with benchmarks for each. This organization enables study of radar-containing multimodal perception across distinct sensing configurations. The main contribution is a large-scale real-world resource that makes 4D radar available for cooperative-perception research alongside established camera and LiDAR modalities.
neurips-2025-v2x-radar-a-multi-modal-dat.tldr: V2X-Radar provides real-world radar, LiDAR, and camera data with benchmarks for cooperative, roadside, and single-vehicle perception.

paragraphs: Rehearsal learning studies how to choose actions that prevent a predicted undesirable outcome. Existing methods address success in a single round, while this paper considers decisions that must coordinate several future outcomes. It extends the Avoiding Undesired Future objective to include relationships between variables across time, making long-term consequences part of the decision target.

Direct optimization of the resulting avoidance probability is difficult. The authors derive an explicit objective and reformulate the problem as quadratic programming. Under mild assumptions, they prove that solutions to this tractable reformulation are equivalent to solutions of the original probabilistic optimization. This gives a computational route to the extended objective.

The paper develops a greedy method that maximizes each round's avoidance probability and a far-sighted method that accounts for future consequences. Its analysis links the latter to a higher overall avoidance probability through an L/(L+1) variance reduction in the objective. An O(1/√N) excess-risk bound addresses decisions made with estimated parameters, and experiments validate the approach's effectiveness.
neurips-2025-variance-reduced-long-term-.tldr: The paper reformulates long-term undesirable-outcome avoidance as quadratic programming and develops greedy and variance-reducing far-sighted decision methods.

paragraphs: Few-shot learning recognizes new classes from only a handful of labeled examples. Language descriptions can add useful information, but descriptions that contradict the actual images introduce misleading guidance. VT-FSL addresses this by conditioning an LLM on both class names and support images, grounding its textual information in the instances available for the task.

Cross-modal Iterative Prompting refines class descriptions within a single structured reasoning pass. Those descriptions also enable zero-shot synthesis of semantically consistent images. Text supplies high-level class information, while the generated images add visual variation within classes. Both become complementary prompts alongside the limited original support data.

Cross-modal Geometric Alignment then jointly aligns textual, support-image, and synthetic-image representations by minimizing the kernelized volume of the three-dimensional parallelotope they span. This objective captures global and nonlinear relationships across the representations. VT-FSL reports new state-of-the-art performance on ten benchmarks covering standard, cross-domain, and fine-grained few-shot learning. The results support combining instance-grounded semantic generation with explicit geometric alignment of the resulting modalities.
neurips-2025-vt-fsl-bridging-vision-and-.tldr: VT-FSL grounds LLM descriptions in support images and geometrically aligns text and visual prompts, achieving leading results across ten few-shot benchmarks.

paragraphs: Critically damped Langevin diffusion models extend a generative process by coupling data coordinates with auxiliary variables. Inspired by Hamiltonian dynamics, these methods have shown numerical advantages over standard diffusion samplers. This paper studies a generalized version of those dynamics, aiming to understand sampling error and how the extended space can be used more effectively.

The generalization adds a hyperparameter controlling the noise applied directly to the data coordinate. This parameter affects the smoothness of sample paths, making it relevant to the behavior of the continuous process and its numerical approximation. The authors derive a new upper bound on sampling error measured in the Wasserstein metric, which compares generated and target distributions.

Their discretization analysis connects the added parameter to errors arising when continuous dynamics are implemented through numerical steps. This connection supplies practical guidance for choosing the parameter and leads to improved sampling performance. The contribution therefore combines a more flexible diffusion process with a theoretical analysis that informs a concrete sampling-design choice.
neurips-2025-wasserstein-convergence-of-.tldr: The paper bounds sampling error for generalized critically damped Langevin diffusions and uses discretization analysis to guide noise-parameter tuning.

paragraphs: Language models can demonstrate mathematical reasoning, yet the internal basis of that capability remains unclear. This paper asks whether reasoning depends on the model broadly, particular modules, or overfitting. Its central hypothesis is that the output projection module, called o_proj, within multi-head self-attention plays a primary role in reasoning in well-trained LLMs.

To investigate, the authors introduce Stethoscope for Networks, a collection of diagnostic tools for probing model internals. They use these tools to assemble circumstantial and empirical evidence suggesting a central role for o_proj. Their analysis also suggests that other modules contribute more strongly to fluent dialogue, motivating a distinction between the internal contributions to these capabilities.

The findings are presented as support for the hypothesis, rather than proof that reasoning resides exclusively in one module. Their significance is a more targeted perspective on interpretability and capability development. If this perspective guides effective training strategies, it could help produce more efficient or specialized models; the abstract presents those training benefits as potential future directions.
neurips-2025-who-reasons-in-the-large-la.tldr: Diagnostic evidence suggests that attention's output projection plays a central role in LLM reasoning, supporting a hypothesis for more targeted training.

paragraphs: Feed-forward 3D Gaussian Splatting models can produce novel views in one pass without optimizing separately for each scene. Their encoders, however, struggle as the number of input views grows, causing degraded performance or excessive memory use. ZPressor addresses this bottleneck by compressing multi-view information into a compact latent state.

The approach is motivated by the Information Bottleneck principle: preserve essential scene information while removing redundancy. It divides input views into anchor and support sets, then uses cross-attention to compress information from support views into the anchors. The resulting state becomes a compact representation of the multi-view input. The module is lightweight and designed for integration across architectures.

With ZPressor, existing feed-forward models can handle more than 100 input views at 480P resolution on an 80GB GPU. Integrations into several leading models consistently improve performance with moderate view counts and robustness with dense views on DL3DV-10K and RealEstate10K. The findings support compression at the encoder bottleneck as a way to make additional views useful without passing their full redundancy through the model.
neurips-2025-zpressor-bottleneck-aware-c.tldr: ZPressor compresses multi-view scene information to improve feed-forward 3DGS performance and support more than 100 input views in the stated hardware setting.
